name: Linen suit

card.summary: A linen suit is breathable summer tailoring made from flax fabric that keeps wearers cooler in heat while giving a relaxed, tailored look.
card.note: Linen wrinkles easily, which many wearers treat as part of the look.

quick.overview:
A linen suit is a jacket and trousers made from linen, a fabric woven from flax fibres. It looks smart in hot weather because the cloth is absorbent, dries quickly and feels cool, so a person can wear tailoring in summer without looking overheated.

Style-wise, linen gives a relaxed texture, and its natural creasing is considered part of its character. Light tan or cream shades are common in summer.
quick.how: Wearers choose linen for warm-weather events and travel, often in lighter shades, and pair it with a simple shirt. Fit and tailoring still shape the silhouette, as with any suit.
quick.risks: Linen wrinkles easily and costs more than cotton to produce. Fully synthetic blends feel warmer than natural fibres.

lead: A linen suit is a suit tailored from linen, the textile made from the bast fibres of the flax plant, worn in warm weather.[1][2]

Wikipedia describes linen as strong and absorbent, quick to dry, and "comfortable to wear in hot weather".[1] Because it has poor elasticity it wrinkles easily, and many modern garments are made to be worn without ironing, treating the creasing as part of its character.[1]
Wikipedia's article on suits lists linen as the main fabric for hot weather, with lighter shades such as tan or cream popular in summer.[2]

chain: Linen is breathable and cool to the touch
Wearer stays comfortable in tailoring in heat
angle.text: A linen suit lets someone dress formally in heat without heavy wool. Its texture and lighter colours give a relaxed look, while fit and tailoring still shape the silhouette.

paras: Linen absorbs moisture well, dries faster than cotton and feels cool to the touch because of higher thermal conductivity; it softens with washing but is more expensive to produce than cotton.[1]

Summer wool suits use lighter cloth, while linen is the main hot-weather option; in the American South cotton seersucker is also worn, and wool blends are used for travel.[2] Light colours are common in summer, and the suit's silhouette depends on tailoring choices such as darts, padding and canvas.[2]
